svg.title: Flow telemetry as the security searchlight: the four questions it answers, the export pipeline, the engineering numbers, and what it cannot do
svg.desc: Left: the four questions only flow data answers - which internal hosts talk to suspicious external addresses, meaning they may already be compromised; which hosts are scanning laterally, meaning they may be infected; who is consuming the egress bandwidth, denial of service or business; and did the policy take effect, which is answered by the hit counters on the deny entries. Middle: the pipeline from devices exporting sampled flow records over UDP to a collector that stores them, an analyser that keeps a baseline and detects anomalies, and an action - alert, black hole, or a policy change. Right: the engineering numbers that decide whether the project survives - sampling of one in a thousand on high-speed links so that the collector is not overwhelmed, an active timeout of about five minutes and an inactive timeout of fifteen seconds, and retention split between raw flows for a week or a month and aggregates for a year. Bottom: what flow data cannot do - it has no payload, so it cannot see content or file names; no domain names, so it cannot tell you the site, only the address; no blocking, so it needs a separate enforcement path; and for encrypted traffic it still yields volume, timing and peer relationships, which is often enough for detection and never enough for proof.
svg.text: Flow telemetry: the cheapest security control nobody budgets for
Firewalls and ACLs decide what may happen. Flow data is the only thing that tells you what is happening right now
FOUR QUESTIONS THAT HAVE NO OTHER ANSWER

g.text: Which internal hosts talk to suspicious
external addresses - are we already owned?
Which hosts scan their peers - where is
Did the policy take effect - what do the

svg.text: Without flow data every one of these becomes a packet capture session
on a single link, at the speed of the slowest engineer awake.
THE PIPELINE · EXPORT, STORE, BASELINE, ACT
Devices
routers, switches,
firewalls, cloud VPC
Exporter
sampled records,
UDP - no delivery
Collector
deduplicate, store,
retention policy
Analyser
baseline + rules,
then alert
The last arrow is the one that gets forgotten: an alert nobody acts on is expensive
telemetry. Wire the analyser to something that can do work - a ticket, an automation,
or a black hole trigger with a named approver.
A design smell
Collector deployed, retention 24 hours,
no baseline. It answers none of the four
A design that works
90 days of raw flows, weekly reports of the
top talkers, one alert per suspicious peer
THE NUMBERS THAT DECIDE THE PROJECT
sampling 1:1000 on 100G links - full flow there saturates any collector
active timeout 300 s · inactive timeout 15 s - shorter means volume, longer
means you cannot see short scans at all
Retention: 7-30 days raw for investigation, 12 months aggregates for trends
Ask for the record-per-second estimate before you buy storage, not after
WHAT FLOW DATA CANNOT DO
No payload - no content, no file name, no command
No domain name - the address only, not the site
No blocking - enforcement is a separate path
Encrypted traffic still gives volume, timing and peer relationships, which is
enough for detection and never enough for proof on its own
Design rule:
every enforcement point should export counters, and every deny rule should be readable as a number. A control you cannot measure is a control you cannot defend in a review.

Cost note: the licence, not the bandwidth, is usually the real constraint - decide the retention and the sampling rate before the vendor shortlist, because both are negotiable and neither is retrofittable.
